overview: The Medford School Committee approved an expansion plan for afterschool programming, established a new Chief Operations Officer position, and approved a five-year copier contract. The committee also debated proposals to increase flexibility for high school health and physical education requirements, delaying a final decision to the next meeting.

items.title: Consent Agenda and Minutes
items.summary: Approved the consent agenda, which included middle and vocational school field trips and the minutes of the May 5, 2025 regular meeting.

items.title: Afterschool Programming Expansion Plan
items.summary: Approved a plan to expand elementary afterschool capacity and eliminate waitlists by forming a task force and partnering with the Belmont After School Enrichment Collaborative (BASIC) for a one-year consultancy.

items.title: Health and Physical Education Requirements
items.summary: Continued the discussion on proposed revisions to physical education and health graduation requirements to the next regular meeting, with an amendment to increase student elective flexibility.

items.title: Chief Operations Officer Job Description
items.summary: Approved the job description for a new Chief Operations Officer position to manage facilities, technology, and security, with amendments clarifying supervisory duties.

items.title: Five-Year Copier Contract
items.summary: Approved a five-year contract with RICO to consolidate district printing devices and integrate PaperCut secure print management software.

items.title: Budget Transfers
items.summary: Approved 10 budget transfers totaling $132,789.46, including funds to cover higher-than-expected unemployment tax charges.

items.title: Summer Programming Rate Card
items.summary: Approved the rate card and design for the summer 2025 MAPS academic enrichment program and the literacy acceleration program.

items.title: Concussion Policy First Reading
items.summary: Approved the first reading of a revised concussion policy to update training, pre-participation requirements, and return-to-play protocols.
